convention: This file carries POINTERS AND TRAPS, not retellings. A задача is cited by its section in PLAN.md or SPEC.md, never paraphrased here: a paraphrase is a second copy of the truth and it drifts (it already did once, for routing_lists). What belongs here instead: file and symbol pointers, measured facts, rejected shapes with their arguments, and the traps that cost the last passes time. Written down in full in implementation-notes.md, section 'doclint — утверждение документа о состоянии обязано опираться на исполнимое'.

measurement_vs_inference.rule: A measurement and the conclusion drawn from it are TWO statements, and this file must keep them apart. Record what was run and what it printed; record separately what you concluded, and name the steps between. A conclusion written as if it were the measurement is inherited by the next pass as measured fact.
measurement_vs_inference.why_this_block_exists: The previous HANDOFF said, citing a live run, that the agent holds the store's exclusive flock for its whole life and therefore `hop nodes` refuses while the tunnel is up. The run was real and still reproduces: `flock -x <root>/.lock sleep 8 &` then `hop nodes` → exit 1 after 5043 ms. The conclusion was wrong, and two inference steps did the damage: (1) 'the agent holds the store' → 'the agent holds the lock' — `store.Open` takes no lock, `load()` reads all three files without one, and the lock lives inside `transact`, per transaction (measured: 559 transactions, mean 1.05 ms); (2) 'the lock is held' → 'a reader waits' — a reader takes no lock at all. Both steps were invisible because the sentence read like a measurement.
measurement_vs_inference.this_round_repeated_it_on_a_test_harness: The controller spent real time chasing a phantom L3 failure in TestW71: `HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn /tmp/l3.test` run from the CONTROLLER's ambient shell, whose cwd had silently reset to the wrong worktree (main, pre-fix) between commands. `internal/l3`'s buildOnce (harness_test.go) rebuilds `hop`/`hopd` from `repoRoot(t)`, computed from `os.Getwd()` AT RUN TIME — not from wherever the already-compiled test binary itself was built. So the compiled test binary was correct, the SOURCE it rebuilt its subject binaries from was not, and the failure reproduced 100% of the time until the invocation was wrapped in `(cd <worktree> && ...)`. Lesson for L3 specifically: always invoke `HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn ...` inside a `(cd <worktree> && ...)` subshell, never after a bare `cd`, and never trust the ambient shell cwd for it.

closed_this_pass.measured_after: Same invocation: client socket opens immediately, `hop status --json` answers with the agent's own picture and exit 3 (fail-close §5.6, NOT 'unavailable'), process alive at 2.5s, SIGTERM gives exit 0. closed_this_pass.decision_where: cmd/hop/transport.go (`lazyControl`), NOT a new internal/supervisor package. Argument: the agent already survives the service DYING (watchService, internal/agent/wire.go, Р34, which explicitly says exiting would make autostart a restart loop) — 'service missing' meaning something different before the first connection than after was the actual defect, i.e. this is symmetry, not a new subsystem. Also: §3.4 already renamed supervisor→agent (PLAN.md D12), so the name is already spent in this product. docs/not-yet-written.md's `internal/supervisor` line stays (the path still doesn't exist) with this choice recorded in it, so it isn't reopened.
closed_this_pass.shape: lazyControl connects on first use, not on the first line of runAgent, and the connection is established AT MOST ONCE — no reconnect after loss, because a control-connection drop is a §6.2 edge the service reads as 'agent gone', and dialing again over an already-orphaned tunnel would start a second session that knows nothing of the first (internal/ipc's own Client comment says this). The wait (svc.wait, only inside the shouldAutoUp branch — an agent with autoconnect off owes the service nothing until `hop up`) has NO deadline of its own by design: only SIGTERM ends it (signal.NotifyContext moved above the autoconnect branch specifically so a wait with no deadline still hears systemctl stop). Retry interval is serviceRetry = 500ms, chosen as a poll (not a filesystem watch) because the Windows named-pipe socket has no directory to watch at all — a successful dial is the one signal common to all three platforms.
closed_this_pass.four_negative_controls: (1) wait() returns on first dial failure instead of looping → both L1 checks red ('ожидание кончилось, хотя сервиса нет'). (2) get() loses its memoization, dials every call → the one-connection assertion reds ('dial позван ещё N раз'). (3) runAgent reverted to the old synchronous c.connect(o.socket) → L3 reds with the EXACT original message. (4) The wiring is pulled — lazyControl exists but run() calls a.Up() directly, skipping svc.wait() → `go test ./cmd/hop` stays FULLY GREEN, only L3 catches it. This last one is the reason the L1/L3 split exists at all (same hole W67 had before W68 closed it).

parallel_passes_trap.new_this_round_a_formatter_mangles_confl: A PostToolUse save-hook in this repo reformats implementation-notes.md on every Edit (table realignment, `*em*`→`_em_`, confirmed content-preserving by the probe-timeout-vs-fail pass's own diff check). It ALSO reformats raw `<<<<<<<`/`=======`/`>>>>>>>` conflict markers left in the file mid-resolution — turning `>>>>>>> <sha>` into `> > > > > > > <sha>` (Markdown blockquote-izing the `>` run) — which means grepping for `^>>>>>>>` after a partial resolution can miss a marker the hook already mangled. gate.rule_learned: The L3 line is part of the gate, not an optional extra — a pass that changed only the CLI surface (ef9027d) once left the whole internal/l3 package red and the other five commands did not see it. Any pass touching cmd/hop, internal/ipc or internal/agent must run it, and the controller must re-run it on the MERGED tree. This round adds a second rule, controller-side: run it via `(cd <worktree> && HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn ...)` in one subshell — see measurement_vs_inference above for what a bare invocation after an earlier `cd` actually tests.

notes.doclint: Fast. CI runs it as `go run ./cmd/doclint -git=false .` — a checkout has neither the pass branches nor the full history, so the git half is off there and on locally.
notes.negcheck: runs every guard twice (with/without its policy) via `go test -count=1`; 48 policies as of last measurement, ~25-35 min wall clock — expected, not a hang; don't rely on go test's cache. It needs permission to listen on loopback: a network-restricted sandbox creates false oracle defects. There is no per-policy selection: for a per-task gate run the new policy's own guard under HOP_DISABLE=<name> by hand; the controller runs the full one at the end. TWO TRAPS MEASURED, both from running it in the background while working. (1) It races your edits: negcheck re-runs `go test` for ~30 minutes, so a tree edited mid-run gets compiled half-edited and the report is a wall of «ДЕФЕКТ ОРАКУЛА … undefined: slices» that says nothing about any policy. Start it only on a tree you have stopped touching. (2) It is load, and load is what the gate's flakes need: `go test ./...` beside a running negcheck is what exposed the W66 flake two rounds ago — useful on purpose, ruinous by accident, because a red then has two possible authors.
notes.realtimelint: does not accept ./... as an argument — pass literally `.`
notes.l3_how_to_run: `go test -c -o /tmp/l3.test ./internal/l3` then `HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn /tmp/l3.test` (add `-test.v -test.run '<pattern>'` to scope it), invoked from inside the worktree whose source you mean to test — see the gate.rule_learned addition above; a bare invocation after an earlier bare `cd` silently tests whatever tree the shell's cwd currently points at, not the tree you built the binary from. No root needed — unshare -Urn grants CAP_NET_ADMIN in a fresh netns. Reuse the built binary across runs. WITHOUT -test.v the package prints only a final PASS, and a fully-skipped package prints the same PASS: count `--- PASS` lines (23 as of this round, zero SKIP) before believing it ran. Name what unshare does NOT isolate: $HOME (hence per-test HOP_STORE) and $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (hence per-test -client-socket).
notes.known_red_that_is_not_yours: go vet ./... is red at internal/engine/dialer.go (copylocks in xray-core's SocketConfig). realtimelint is red with 3 hits in internal/dnstest/realserver_test.go (SetReadDeadline on real sockets — confirmed AGAIN this round, still deliberate, dnstest-port-collision pass checked and didn't touch that file). gofmt -l ./internal reports internal/l2/dns_test.go. All three predate every pass touching them; the honest gate is 'no NEW findings', compared on the full output rather than the exit code. Capture the baseline before starting — it makes acceptance a diff instead of a judgement.
notes.flake: Three found and fixed across three rounds, none about clocks; unchanged this round (nothing in this round's four passes touched internal/l2, internal/health's probe timing outside the A36 fix which was regression-checked against A22 directly, or internal/agent's persist path). internal/l2 TestT10SlowNodeKeepsConnectionAlive: 0 red in 400 runs under 16 busy loops (was 8 of 200). internal/health TestA22PinnedNodeIsNotReplacedWhenDead: 0 red in 5×10 under -race (was 2 of 3), and re-confirmed 10/10 green this round after the A36 classification change touched the same function. internal/agent TestW66NodesCarryLiveHealthNotTheDiskSlice: 0 red in 160 runs under load (was 4 of 5 runs × 20). The pattern all three share: the test waited for an event that is not the one it needed, and the missing wait was invisible on an idle machine.
notes.what_is_not_a_flake: cmd/hop/measure_test.go compares against time in exactly one place — `hop nodes` must return 0 — and the margin there is three orders of magnitude. A refusal in that test is a regression, not load. The 'longest held' numbers it logs are not assertions and move freely on a busy machine.
notes.negative_control_on_l3_can_lie: internal/l3 builds `hop` and `hopd` itself (buildOnce, harness_test.go) and FAILS the test on a build error — UNLESS HOP_L3_BIN_HOP / HOP_L3_BIN_HOPD are set, and then it silently uses the binaries they name. So a hand-made break that does not COMPILE gives a GREEN L3 run against the previous binary. When reddening an L3 guard by hand: either unset HOP_L3_BIN_*, or rebuild them after every edit, and make the break compile. RELATED, measured THIS round the hard way (see measurement_vs_inference): buildOnce resolves its build root from `os.Getwd()` at RUN TIME via repoRoot(t), not from wherever the test binary itself was compiled — so even a correctly-built test binary will rebuild `hop`/`hopd` from the WRONG source tree if invoked with the wrong ambient cwd. Same failure mode as the stale-binary trap, opposite cause: this one silently tests the RIGHT test logic against the WRONG subject binary.
notes.fake_clock_hole_left_open: clock.Fake.After(d) with d <= 0 never fires on its own, while the real time.After(0) fires immediately. Deliberately not fixed: the fix would make the number of probe-loop turns unpredictable, and T6 and A24 assert on that count. Verified by reading internal/clock/fake.go. Anyone hitting a fake-clock test that hangs should look here first — and note the dnstest.Clock wrapper (internal/dnstest/clock.go, WaitAfterCalls) is the project's answer to the OTHER half of this problem (advancing a fake clock before the goroutine under test has actually reached its wait) — the D45 fix this round is a second user of that exact pattern, cite it as a worked example before reinventing the synchronization.

autostart_decision.what_was_decided: §6.13's second and third thirds (autostart of the SERVICE and of the AGENT), decided by the human two rounds ago after the facts below were gathered, then implemented (packaging pass) and its exposed defect closed (this round, W71).
autostart_decision.facts_that_shaped_it: (1) Nothing about packaging existed in the repo before the packaging pass: no Makefile, no scripts, no unit/plist/wxs, dist/ is gitignored. (2) hopd has no service-manager integration at all — flags -socket /run/hop.sock, -group hop, -ready-file, foreground, SIGTERM → teardown + snapshot verify; no sd_notify, no socket activation, no SCM. (3) macOS and Windows dataplanes are honest errors from platform.New(), so an installer for them cannot be tested here.
autostart_decision.decision_1_scope: Units + a dev-install script only; .deb/.rpm/.pkg/MSI stay queued — the packages arrive with the platforms that can be tested. Implemented: packaging/systemd/hopd.service, packaging/systemd/hop-agent.service, packaging/install.sh.
autostart_decision.decision_2_registration: Declarative: unit files shipped as FILES, no `hop service install` verb. Implemented as decided.
autostart_decision.decision_3_agent_at_login: `systemctl --global enable hop-agent.service` — the install script enables the user unit for every user session, per §8.5 I1. Implemented as decided.
autostart_decision.decision_4_group: The install creates group `hop` and adds $SUDO_USER to it. Implemented as decided.
autostart_decision.what_this_exposed_and_is_now_fixed: Autostart at login turned 'the agent doesn't wait for the service' into a restart loop: a login racing hopd got an agent that died at once, RestartSec=2s bought roughly ten seconds before the unit went failed. FIXED this round — see closed_this_pass, 'Агент не переживает недоступный сервис' (W71, head 04276c1). The agent now stays alive, answers `hop status` with fail-close code 3, and attaches when the service appears; packaging/systemd/hop-agent.service's RestartSec=2s comment has been rewritten to say so and to name what (weaker) argument keeps the number in place.
autostart_decision.verification_available_here: `systemd-analyze verify` exists on this machine (systemd 261) and needs no root and no installation. There is NO container runtime (no docker, no podman). Unit files are verified by systemd-analyze; the install script against a staging DESTDIR; the REAL install (`sudo`, enable --now, is-active, removal) only in .github/workflows/install-linux.yml on a disposable runner, unverified locally — same status l3-macos.yml/l3-windows.yml carry, and it has still never run (this repository does not push).
autostart_decision.implemented_by: de922ac (units, install script), 04276c1 (W71 fix to the defect they exposed). This block stays because the decision's REASONS are not repeated in the units themselves, only its shape.
